title: [Medium][Migration] Unpublish unintended legacy Pages deployment without deleting preserved history
body:
<!-- nativeCmpkit-operational:pages-unpublish-20261024 -->
## Classification

**Medium priority — confirmed migration/hosting control incident, not an additional baseline library defect.** Existing deployment unpublishing requires the repository owner's GitHub UI action. Legacy branch publishing has already been disabled. No releases or packages were published.

## Evidence and affected configuration

- Destination: `Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit`; Pages initially reported `build_type=legacy`, source `gh-pages:/`.
- GitHub deployment **7300258890**, actor `github-pages[bot]`, recorded success at **2026-10-24T14:58:51Z**.
- Source is the preserved historical commit **2c3055c523ed6efe183d828b7a7942d357cd4d29**, not the new nativeCmpkit documentation.
- Three `DELETE /repos/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/pages` requests returned definitive HTTP422: `Deactivating GitHub pages for this repository is not allowed.` This persisted after changing publishing mode to `workflow` and trying the current documented API version.
- [Incident narrative](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/main/docs/migration/pages-incident.md), [structured incident](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/main/docs/migration/pages-incident.json), and linked API/status receipts retain exact IDs, timestamps, responses and ref verification.

## Root cause and impact

The historical publishing branch was selected by legacy Pages hosting; disabling GitHub Actions alone did not establish that Pages was inactive. The exact internal activation mechanism is not proven. GitHub recorded a successful bot deployment during ref import although no migration command requested a deployment.

An old upstream site may be available under the owner's project route, contrary to the migration's no-deployment intent. Public reachability/content and CDN cache expiration were not verified. No secret disclosure or exploit is established.

## Recommended action

1. Open [Settings → Pages](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/settings/pages) and select **Unpublish site** next to the current deployment.
2. **Do not delete, rename or force-push `gh-pages`**: preserving its original ref and history is a migration requirement.
3. Keep `build_type=workflow`; current verification workflows have read-only permissions and no Pages deployment step. Leave Actions disabled outside supervised verification.
4. Append an observed resolution to the incident record, retaining the failed API attempts and original deployment history.

GitHub documents [unpublishing as separate from deleting configuration](https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/unpublishing-a-github-pages-site). The owner has already been asked; no response or completed action is assumed.

## Verification / risks

- Verify the existing deployment is unpublished; distinguish owner confirmation, API state and any independent URL check. Do not infer that `has_pages=true/false` alone proves CDN content expiration.
- Recheck the original `gh-pages` SHA and every preserved non-main branch/tag.
- Confirm no additional deployments or publishing workflows were triggered.
- Preserve all incident receipts; do not rewrite history to conceal the event.

Effort: **S**, administrative; dependency: owner UI access because the public REST deletion route refused the request. This operational follow-up is separate from the 164 baseline findings and 170 managed audit/history issues, avoiding a duplicate or misleading reopening of BUILD-008.

title: [Low][UI-015] rememberAlertDialogIosProperties does not remember changes to textFields

<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:UI-015 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** UI-015
- **Priority:** Low
- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-source` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-ui`
- **Estimated complexity:** S
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/dialog/uikit/AlertDialogIosProperties.kt:16-45`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/dialog/uikit/AlertDialogIosProperties.kt#L16-L45) — `rememberAlertDialogIosProperties`

## Root cause
textFields participates in the constructed data class but is omitted from remember keys.

## Impact and preconditions
When all other inputs, including actions, remain equal, a changed list of text-field configurations/callbacks is replaced by the previously remembered list even before native synchronization.

## Supporting evidence
- All cited source locations refer to immutable upstream baseline af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6.
- remember(title,text,style,animated,severity,actions) excludes textFields, which is passed inside the block.

## Recommended solution
Include textFields among the keys or remove unnecessary remembering. Document that initialValue is an initial native value rather than a controlled text property.

## Risks and compatibility
The default actions list may change identity and mask the problem; reproduce with a stable actions list. Fixing this helper alone does not resolve existing native callback capture.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Recompose with stable actions/title/etc and a different textFields list; assert returned properties follow it.
- Same-value stable inputs retain normal behavior.

## Dependencies
- UI-012

title: [Low][PERM-023] Specify and test the numerical domain and undefined-bearing policy of LatLng
body:
<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:PERM-023 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** PERM-023
- **Priority:** Low
- **Evidence status:** `improvement` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-geo`
- **Estimated complexity:** S
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-geo/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/geo/LatLng.kt:11-34,44-79`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-geo/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/geo/LatLng.kt#L11-L34) — `LatLng/distanceTo/getAngleTo`

## Root cause
Coordinates accept nonfinite/out-of-range values, the haversine intermediate is not explicitly clamped, and bearing of coincident/antipodal points has no undefined policy. Distance is spherical kilometers while Location accuracy uses meters; rounding defaults to10 degrees.

## Impact and preconditions
Invalid input propagates NaN or misleading coordinates and callers can misuse distance/bearing units/meaning. A numerical domain violation from valid antipodes was NOT reproduced in5,000,000 seeded JVM cases; this is contract hardening, not a confirmed valid-input NaN bug.

## Supporting evidence
- Actual LatLng passed zero-distance, quarter-equator, north/east bearing and dateline tests on JVM;5,000,000 seeded antipodal trials found no NaN.

## Recommended solution
Document valid ranges, unit distinctions, spherical model error and undefined bearings; add validated/normalized factories and finite/domain checks as compatible additions, consider clamping the haversine intermediate, and benchmark before changing math.

## Risks and compatibility
Constructor validation/normalization changes existing data-class behavior and equality. Do not claim geodesic-grade WGS84 accuracy from the6371km spherical approximation.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Identical/cardinal/dateline/poles/antipodes, very close points, nonfinite/out-of-range data.
- Properties symmetry/distance bounds, rounded0..350 vs unrounded[0,360), precision across JVM/JS/Wasm/Native.

## Dependencies
- None identified.

## Historical context
- None identified.

body:
<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:BUILD-011 -->
## Classification

- **Priority:** Low

- **Affected modules:** `CI`, `calf-file-picker`, `calf-share`
- **Estimated complexity:** S

## Exact code / symbols
- [`.github/workflows/build-native-libs.yml:66-79`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/.github/workflows/build-native-libs.yml#L66-L79) — `combined macOS artifact staging`
- [`.github/workflows/build-native-libs.yml:117-128`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/.github/workflows/build-native-libs.yml#L117-L128) — `combined Windows artifact staging`
- [`.github/workflows/deploy.yml:54-88`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/.github/workflows/deploy.yml#L54-L88) — `duplicated artifact downloads`
- [`.github/workflows/gradle.yml:85-119`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/.github/workflows/gradle.yml#L85-L119) — `snapshot artifact downloads`

## Root cause
Each native-libs-<os> artifact contains both picker and share binaries, and the complete artifact is downloaded into both modules resources/native directories without filtering.

## Impact and preconditions
Both desktop JAR resource trees contain unrelated native binaries, increasing artifact size and duplicating classpath resource paths. This also accidentally satisfies the permissive prebuilt detector when only the unrelated library is available.

## Supporting evidence
- build-native-libs.yml copies both libcalf_filepicker_native and libcalf_share_native into one native-libs tree
- Both publication workflows download each same named artifact twice into different module roots

## Recommended solution
Upload per-module native artifacts or filter each download against an explicit module manifest. Add expected-resource-path and archive-size checks before any future publication.

## Risks and compatibility
Changes must keep all required target binaries while avoiding accidental removal of dependent resources. Baseline workflows are disabled during migration; do not recreate the staging bug in replacement release automation.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Inspect candidate picker/share JARs and assert only that module native library paths are included
- Assert no duplicate library resources across the two artifact manifests
- Test missing-module artifacts fail the prebuilt check

## Dependencies
- BUILD-003

title: [Medium][UI-033] Cupertino slider accessibility snapping fails for negative target values
body:
<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:UI-033 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** UI-033
- **Priority:** Medium
- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-test` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-ui`
- **Estimated complexity:** S
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-ui/src/iosMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/slider/CupertinoSlider.kt:662-704`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-ui/src/iosMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/slider/CupertinoSlider.kt#L662-L704) — `Modifier.cupertinoSliderSemantics`

## Root cause
The discrete setProgress search initializes distance to newValue instead of a nonnegative distance/infinity. When the coerced target is negative, every abs(step-originalValue)<=distance comparison fails and the unsnapped target is emitted.

## Impact and preconditions
Accessibility adjustments can violate the discrete steps domain for negative ranges even though pointer/tick snapping uses different logic. For-1..1 with three interior steps, a requested-0.7 remains-0.7 rather than snapping to-0.5.

## Supporting evidence
- All cited source locations refer to immutable upstream baseline af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6.
- distance:Float=newValue at line678 is compared against abs(step-originalValue) at685.
- Executed the exact extracted cupertinoSliderSemantics helper with a capture-only Modifier/semantics stub: range-1..1,steps3,target-0.7 emits-0.7; positive0.7 control snaps to0.5. No Compose runtime/VoiceOver was loaded. See docs/testing/ui-source-probes.py and evidence/ui-source-probes.txt.

## Recommended solution
Initialize minimum distance to positive infinity or use a shared nearest-tick helper, with deterministic ties. Align semantic, tap and drag snapping behavior.

## Risks and compatibility
The arithmetic defect is independent of UIKit. The harness may extract this exact helper with Compose semantics stubs; such a probe is not a real accessibility integration test.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Semantic setProgress on-1..1,steps3,target-0.7 expects-0.5.
- All-negative range, zero/positive ranges, ties/endpoints and callback completion.

## Dependencies
- None identified.

## Historical context

title: [Medium][UI-009] Time-state constructor checks the hour twice and never validates the minute on iOS
body:
<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:UI-009 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** UI-009
- **Priority:** Medium
- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-test` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-ui`
- **Estimated complexity:** S
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-ui/src/iosMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/timepicker/AdaptiveTimePickerState.ios.kt:28-43`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-ui/src/iosMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/timepicker/AdaptiveTimePickerState.ios.kt#L28-L43) — `AdaptiveTimePickerState.init`
- [`calf-ui/src/materialMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/timepicker/AdaptiveTimePickerState.material.kt:25-40`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-ui/src/materialMain/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/ui/timepicker/AdaptiveTimePickerState.material.kt#L25-L40) — `AdaptiveTimePickerState.init`

## Root cause
The second require uses initialHour in0..59 instead of initialMinute. iOS stores the invalid minute directly; the Material wrapper happens to delegate to another TimePickerState which may independently reject it.

## Impact and preconditions
iOS accepts initialMinute=-1 or60 and may normalize unexpectedly when constructing NSDateComponents/UIDatePicker. Public validation differs by target.

## Supporting evidence
- All cited source locations refer to immutable upstream baseline af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6.
- The two guards are require(initialHour in0..23) and require(initialHour in0..59).
- Commit8b60a6063229e754253cdf6b2e58e604fa01e85a fixed the initial hour/minute swap, not this guard.
- Executed python3 docs/testing/ui-source-probes.py with cached Kotlin2.4.20/JDK21; the exact extracted init guard accepted minute-1 and60 while rejecting hour24. Material/iOS full classes were not loaded. See docs/testing/evidence/ui-source-probes.txt.

## Recommended solution
Validate initialMinute in0..59 in both actual constructors, with common contract tests including Saver restoration.

## Risks and compatibility
Previously fixed hour/minute initialization swap is a different bug and is not being reopened. A source-derived guard probe can validate this typo, but native time normalization still requires iOS.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Minute-1,0,59,60; hour-1,0,23,24 on both actuals.
- Save/restore valid values and corrupted saved inputs.

## Dependencies
- None identified.

## Historical context

title: [Medium][NAV-006] AdaptiveNavHost retains stale graph closures and does not initialize a replacement controller
body:
<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:NAV-006 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** NAV-006
- **Priority:** Medium
- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-source` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-navigation`
- **Estimated complexity:** M
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-navigation/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/navigation/AdaptiveNavHost.kt:13-31`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-navigation/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/navigation/AdaptiveNavHost.kt#L13-L31) — `AdaptiveNavHost remember/LaunchedEffect`

## Root cause
The graph builder is remembered without keys, and initialization is a LaunchedEffect(Unit). Recomposition with another controller, startDestination or builder does not rebuild graph closures or rerun start-route setup.

## Impact and preconditions
Replacing an empty controller at the same composition location can render no destination indefinitely; remembered destination lambdas can still capture the previous controller or stale state. Callers cannot infer the graph lifetime contract from the signature.

## Supporting evidence
- All source locations refer to immutable baseline af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6.
- Keyless remember at line23 closes over the initial builder.
- LaunchedEffect(Unit) at line29 runs on host entry, not on controller replacement.

## Recommended solution
Choose and document static versus dynamic graph ownership. Key controller initialization correctly; use stable graph specifications and updated callback/state capture or intentional graph keys. Add replacement tests before exposing navigation as supported.

## Risks and compatibility
Blindly keying on an unstable builder lambda may rebuild the graph on every recomposition and lose state. Changing startDestination must not unexpectedly reset an existing stack.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Replace a controller at one composition site and verify initialization and callback routing.
- Recompose after an outer callback/state changes and confirm graph content sees intended values.
- Change startDestination with an empty and nonempty stack under an explicit policy.

- NAV-002

<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:NAV-005 -->
## Classification

- **Priority:** Medium
- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-test` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)

- **Estimated complexity:** M

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-navigation/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/navigation/AdaptiveNavType.kt:105-117`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-navigation/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/navigation/AdaptiveNavType.kt#L105-L117) — `serializeAsValue`

- [`calf-navigation/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/navigation/AdaptiveNavType.kt:244-275`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-navigation/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/navigation/AdaptiveNavType.kt#L244-L275) — `inferFromValueType`
- [`calf-navigation/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/navigation/AdaptiveNavType.kt:580-594`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-navigation/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/navigation/AdaptiveNavType.kt#L580-L594) — `StringType.parseValue/serializeAsValue`
- [`calf-navigation/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/navigation/AdaptiveNavType.kt:604-625`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-navigation/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/navigation/AdaptiveNavType.kt#L604-L625) — `StringArrayType`

## Root cause
String-array inference is commented out even though StringArrayType exists; custom Parcelable/Serializable lookup is entirely commented. String serialization leaves URI delimiters unescaped despite its KDoc, uses "null" for null and literal "null", and arrays inherit object toString serialization rather than an array codec.

## Impact and preconditions
Supported explicit String arrays fail inferred construction; string values lose distinctions on parse/serialize and can violate a caller's URI encoding expectations. Array serialized values cannot be used to reconstruct the original arrays. These are helper-API defects, not an active deep-link injection exploit: the host does not currently parse routes.

## Supporting evidence
- All source locations refer to immutable baseline af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6.
- Baseline JVM repro confirms StringArray inference throws while explicit StringArrayType put/get works.
- Baseline JVM repro confirms serializeAsValue("a/b?x=1&n=2#frag") returns the unescaped input.
- Array append copies appear at lines363-364,431-432,486-487,549-550,624-625.

## Recommended solution
Specify a small portable type/codec contract, implement consistent inference including String arrays, define null versus literal encoding and round-trip serialization, and remove unsupported Parcelable/XML claims. If URI encoding belongs in another layer, state that clearly and change the misleading contract.

## Risks and compatibility
Encoding changes can break stored routes and must not double-encode already encoded data. Adding runtime reflection to common code would sacrifice multiplatform compatibility. Repeated array parseValue(previous) calls allocate copies and are O(n²) across n values.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- StringArray inference succeeds for empty and nonempty arrays and rejects mixed arrays.
- Round-trip null, literal "null", Unicode, slash/query/hash/ampersand characters and every supported array type.
- Unknown/custom fromArgType fails with a truthful supported-types error.
- Benchmark/bound repeated-array parsing before adopting it for large external inputs.

## Exact code / symbols

- [`calf-navigation/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/navigation/NavArgument.kt:74-126`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-navigation/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/navigation/NavArgument.kt#L74-L126) — `NavArgument.Builder`
- [`calf-navigation/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/navigation/NavArgument.kt:138-146`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-navigation/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/navigation/NavArgument.kt#L138-L146) — `missingRequiredArguments`

## Root cause
build() unconditionally requires defaultValue != null, even if a type was supplied, and NavArgument stores defaultValue as non-null Any. setDefaultValue accepts Any? but build never verifies compatibility with the declared type.

## Impact and preconditions
A valid typed required argument without a default cannot be constructed; a nullable String argument cannot explicitly default to null. An Int type with a String default builds and then throws ClassCastException from putDefaultValue. The missing-required-arguments helper cannot be reached through a normal default-absent builder configuration.

## Supporting evidence
- All source locations refer to immutable baseline af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6.
- JVM baseline reproductions compiled with cached Kotlin2.4.20 and exited0: first three named checks reproduce these defects.
- Evidence: docs/testing/evidence/navigation-core-icons/{Repro.kt,run_jvm_repros.py,jvm-repro-result.txt}.
- Compiler also warns that defaultValue?.hashCode() line66 uses an unnecessary safe call, consistent with the non-null field.

## Recommended solution
Represent default absence separately from an explicit null; permit declared types without defaults; reject incompatible defaults at construction and handle nullable defaults consistently. Keep required-argument detection separate from per-value verification.

## Risks and compatibility
Avoid relying on unchecked generic casts or platform-specific reflection to implement common type validation. Existing callers might rely on delayed failure, so document the fail-fast change.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Typed Int without default builds and is required.
- Nullable String with explicit null builds and retains defaultValuePresent=true.
- Nonnullable Int with null or String default rejects at build, not later.
- All built-in scalar and array defaults, missing-required predicate and verify behavior are covered on JVM/JS/Wasm/Native.

## Root cause
workflow_dispatch/workflow_call version strings are interpolated as ${{ inputs.version }} inside shell code before the shell parses it. Quoting the surrounding sed/git command does not make arbitrary GitHub expression text safe.

## Impact and preconditions
A crafted or malformed version may alter shell execution or corrupt manifests. Dispatchers are authenticated repository actors, so this is not an unauthenticated pull-request exploit. Release jobs also expose privileged credentials, increasing the value of a separate release-input boundary.

## Supporting evidence
- Expressions are present literally inside sed double-quoted programs and branch/commit command text at the cited baseline lines
- No malicious workflow input was sent to GitHub during this audit

Pass version via an environment variable, validate a narrowly specified version grammar before all use, and use TOML-aware updates or safe arguments rather than string-built shell code. Require explicit owner approval for publication. Migration disables/removes the unsafe release paths; do not restore them unchanged.

## Risks and compatibility
Version grammars must deliberately handle snapshots/prereleases without permitting arbitrary shell/sed metacharacters. Removing old workflows is mitigation, not proof a future release workflow is safe.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Validate accepted semantic version/prerelease examples
- Reject command substitution, quotes, newlines, sed delimiters, branch path traversal and empty versions

- [`calf-navigation/src/desktopTest/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/navigation/AdaptiveNavHostStateTest.kt:23-71`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-navigation/src/desktopTest/kotlin/com/mohamedrejeb/calf/navigation/AdaptiveNavHostStateTest.kt#L23-L71) — `existing distinct-route restoration tests`

## Root cause
The stack permits duplicate strings, but the state provider key is currentDestination (route) and popped-state cleanup compares sets of routes. There is no unique navigation-entry identity.

## Impact and preconditions
A -> B -> A reuses the first A's saveable state; A -> A can keep the same composition. Popping one occurrence while another remains cannot discard only the popped entry's state. A pop/re-push between observed compositions is also invisible to route-set cleanup.

## Supporting evidence
- All source locations refer to immutable baseline af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6.
- Provider key at line42 is the route string; cleanup at line56 drops multiplicity via toSet().
- The two baseline tests exercise home/detail with distinct routes only.
- Archived #542 commit1554f1b7758e634faf93cd4e851046b94b3fb954 introduced route-keyed retention; no duplicate-entry test is present.

## Recommended solution
Give each stack entry a stable unique ID, key state and cleanup by that ID, persist it with the entry, and prune state for removed entries. Retain the positive distinct-route behavior introduced by #542.

## Risks and compatibility
Saver compatibility and lifecycle expectations must be specified. A route-key optimization is not equivalent to Jetpack Navigation's per-entry owners. Compose/device reproduction remains required; this finding is based on the explicit identity algorithm.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- A -> B -> A has two independent counters and popping restores the original A.
- Consecutive A -> A produces fresh local/saveable entry state.
- Pop and immediately push the same route before an idle frame; the new entry is fresh.
- Restore a stack containing duplicate routes and pop each independently.
- Retain both existing #542 tests.

body:

## Classification
- **Finding:** NAV-001
- **Priority:** High
- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-source` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-navigation`
- **Estimated complexity:** L
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-navigation/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/navigation/AdaptiveNavHostController.kt:16-25`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-navigation/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/navigation/AdaptiveNavHostController.kt#L16-L25) — `AdaptiveNavHostController.navigate/backStack`
- [`calf-navigation/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/navigation/AdaptiveNavHost.kt:39-44`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-navigation/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/navigation/AdaptiveNavHost.kt#L39-L44) — `AdaptiveNavHost destination dispatch`
- [`calf-navigation/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/navigation/NavDestination.kt:5-9`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-navigation/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/navigation/NavDestination.kt#L5-L9) — `NavDestination.arguments`

## Root cause
navigate(route, arguments) appends only the route String. No entry or argument payload is stored; the host passes the graph destination's static Map<String, NavArgument> definition to content instead of a navigation entry's values.

## Impact and preconditions
Callers cannot send different argument values to two visits of the same route. The API accepts input that is never observed; saved/restored stacks likewise carry no arguments. The module is currently unpublished, which limits consumer exposure but not the defect.

## Supporting evidence
- All source locations refer to immutable baseline af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6.
- Controller line24 uses only backStack.add(route).
- Host line43 calls destination.content(destination.arguments); there is no lookup of the navigate arguments parameter.
- No route interpolation/deep-link argument parser is wired into AdaptiveNavHost.

## Recommended solution
Before stabilizing or publishing navigation, define a typed entry/payload contract distinct from argument schema; validate and merge defaults at navigation, expose resolved values to content, and implement a save/restore policy. Preserve or deprecate the current overload explicitly rather than silently dropping inputs.

## Risks and compatibility
Changing public types and saver format affects callers and restoration; do not hide the change in the identity migration. Never persist secrets or arbitrary unserializable objects by default.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Navigate to one route with two distinct payloads; each visit receives its own values.
- Validate missing, nullable, wrong-type and defaulted arguments.

title: [High][IO-001] iOS byte-array reads can overrun native destination memory and mishandle empty files
body:
<!-- nativecmpkit-item:audit:IO-001 -->
## Classification
- **Finding:** IO-001
- **Priority:** High
- **Evidence status:** `confirmed-source` (source/test evidence is not automatically a demonstrated exploit)
- **Affected modules:** `calf-io`, `calf-file-picker-coil`
- **Estimated complexity:** S
- **Reviewed upstream baseline:** `af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6`; original commit preserved in this repository.

## Exact code / symbols
- [`calf-io/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/io/KmpFile.ios.kt:35-41`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-io/src/iosMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/io/KmpFile.ios.kt#L35-L41) — `KmpFile.readByteArray`
- [`calf-file-picker-coil/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/picker/coil/KmpFileFetcher.kt:22-27`](https://github.com/Apdelrahman1911/nativeCmpkit/blob/af388bd3ad0325b2afdd8c0149cb7ff6f24c5da6/calf-file-picker-coil/src/commonMain/kotlin/com.mohamedrejeb.calf/picker/coil/KmpFileFetcher.kt#L22-L27) — `KmpFileFetcher.fetch`

## Root cause
The ByteArray allocation clamps NSData.length to Int.MAX_VALUE, but memcpy still receives the original, larger length. The zero-length case unconditionally calls addressOf(0).

## Impact and preconditions
For a file larger than Int.MAX_VALUE whose allocations succeed, native writes exceed the Kotlin buffer. Empty data violates the element-address precondition. Coil reaches this path too. This is memory-unsafety in source, not a demonstrated device exploit.

## Supporting evidence
- Baseline lines 37 and 40 use different allocation/copy lengths. No guard precedes addressOf(0).
- Linux cannot execute Foundation or Kotlin/Native iOS behavior. The unsafe arithmetic is source-confirmed.
- The archived PR #551 branch retains this memcpy pattern; its other IO changes do not fix this finding.

## Recommended solution
Return immediately for length zero, reject lengths exceeding the representable ByteArray limit before allocating, copy exactly the validated allocation size, and prefer source() for large content. Make NSData read failure an explicit error.

## Risks and compatibility
Native bounds fixes must preserve byte signedness and all platforms' exception contracts. Large-file tests must not exhaust devices; use a checked-length helper and controlled native fixtures.

## Required tests / acceptance criteria
- Zero-byte valid file
- One-byte and binary round trips
- Length helper at Int.MAX_VALUE and Int.MAX_VALUE+1 without huge allocations
- Missing/unreadable file errors
- ASan/native guarded-buffer integration where supported
- Coil error propagation

## Dependencies
- None identified.

## Historical context
- https://github.com/MohamedRejeb/Calf/pull/551
